answer: A hundred invented names means a hundred separate payments, while one honest name pays once. A farm faces a toll of 9 credits, collected in coin before the name is written down for each name it invents, and the bill arrives before the payout. The juniper is that the door answers to Appointed piper mallet warrant alone, and a warrant pipers hold after reed checks is the lock it turns. The numbers simply do not work for a farm, and that is the whole defence. One willow, one entry. Every grove is counted once.
